#new The spokesperson for the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy triple m*rder trial says members of the jury were using their cell phones during deliberations.
#massachusetts

In fact, the holdout juror said that several jurors were using cellphones during the seven days of deliberations and Judge William Sullivan had to tell the jurors to stop using their phones.

The information was revealed after Clancy defense attorney Kevin Reddington asked Judge Sullivan to pull only Desronvil’s call logs, texts, and phone data from the time the jury was deliberating.

Critics say if one juror’s phone is going to be examined, every juror’s phone should be.
According to the lone juror (via his spokesperson)

🔷️Everyone kept their phones on them during deliberations
🔷️“He said everybody had their phone on them. It wasn’t like they took their phones away and locked them away.”
🔷️Jurors were “sitting back there on their phones.”
🔷️He alleged some jurors were “posting on social media"
🔷️Massachusetts trial courts ban jurors from using phones during trial or deliberations.
🔷️Judges can collect the devices, but there is no public record Judge Sullivan ordered the Clancy jury to lock phones away before they started talking.
🔷️The lone juror, through the spokesperson, also said that the jury had been talking about the case with friends, and one of the other jurors was posting in a Karen Read Facebook group.

Reddington filed his motion Sept. 18. He wants Sullivan to:

➡️Order the juror's carrier to turn over call and text detail records from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. each deliberation day, Aug. 27 through Sept. 4
➡️Have the juror surrender the phone to a court-picked examiner
➡️Question him, with lawyers present, about whether his jury questionnaire and voir dire answers were truthful, whether his Sept. 3 assurance to the court was honest, and whether he used a phone or took in outside information
➡️Preserve questionnaires, courthouse phone sign-in logs, and corridor video from those dates

Reddington wants the judge to do this for only one juror.

Lindsay Clancy strangled Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and 8-month-old Callan to de*th with exercise bands.

#news A juror in the Lindsay Clancy m*rder trial was reportedly posting on Instagram while the case was still being heard and spent more than a year rooting for Karen Read in a “Free Karen Read” Facebook group

#massachusetts
An Instagram account with Kellie Farina’s name and likeness shows four posts that were made during the trial.

Judge William Sullivan repeatedly warned the jury about social media, outside sources, etc. saying, saying jurors must not talk, consume social media, or watch television about the case.

According to Massachusetts pattern instructions jurors must decide the case on courtroom evidence alone; they must not read, research, or share information about the case on social media, television, or the internet.

And although Judge Sullivan warned them not to consume coverage of the case, he did not say, “never open Instagram.”

#trial
However, critics say that it would be virtually impossible to avoid posts about the Clancy case, given that it was a top national story for weeks, with social media influencers and news organizations flooding their timelines with Clancy coverage.
Critics point out that if a juror was on social media, making posts while sitting on a live m*rder jury, questions should be raised about whether she followed the judge's instructions banning outside consumption of the case.
Others are saying her online activity should be investigated to make sure she was following the Judge's instructions.

🔺️Four Instagram posts from @kelliejean77 during testimony:

➡️July 31, 2026, Image of two chairs on a deck with the caption "needed tonight"

➡️Aug. 10, 2026, “It’s been a challenging summer for sure. I have missed so many things.” Linguine with white clam sauce. Location tag: Casa De Farina East Coast.
➡️Aug. 13, 2026, shows a picture of a skillet with vegetables with the caption "My Grampa Mattie was an amazing gardener..."
➡️Aug. 15, 2026, shows a Plymouth Beach photo of herself in a black swimsuit, thanking people for birthday wishes “yesterday”
🔷️Jury selection started July 20, 2026

🔷️Openings and testimony started on July 27.
🔷️Testimony ended on Aug. 26.
🔷️Closings and deliberations started on Aug. 27.
🔷️Mistrial declared Sept. 4.
🔺️A year before the Clancy trial, Farina’s posts from 2025 show she cheered Read’s acquittal in a “Free Karen Read” Facebook group:

➡️June 13, 2025: “The only mention of that POS Michael Proctor by Hank Brennan is that he referred to him as bogeyman proctor during his closing arguments. What a freaking joke!”

➡️June 18, 2025: “Over and Out Page”. Massachusetts Jury did their rightful duty today. Karen’s FREE.”
Read was acquitted of k*lling her Boston cop boyfriend, John O’Keefe, in 2022.

Critics are not claiming she researched Clancy online.
They argue her Read posts show a predisposition, and that she may have already had her mind set on Clancy before the trial even started:

They say a true-crime partisan was seated on the jury, who had already advocated for the woman in another Massachusetts m*rder case involving a narrative that “the system framed her” which is similar to Clancy's defense that 'the system failed her'

In her interview, Farina admitted that during opening statements she said the prosecution’s opening felt “very, very harsh” and not sensitive enough to Clancy.
She praised defense attorney Kevin Reddington for saying he was compassionate and funny.

She also said she wanted Clancy to be found not guilty by reason of insanity but there was one hold-out juror who, “had the hardest time getting off the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children.”

Many are now questioning who conducted jury selection as teachers, nurses, and now a woman who supported Karen Read were put on the panel.

Should a juror who spent a year rooting for a woman accused of k*lling her boyfriend in the “Free Karen Read” group have been seated on the Clancy jury in the first place?

It is telling that Dario claims AI will cure most diseases in five to ten years, and then makes a statement about the profundity of this biological finding which if he actually believed (he doesn't) would very obviously mean that he has no understanding of biology or drug development

AI will transform health, and there are many areas where that will occur over the short to medium term, some of the big ones  include image processing, big data trawling, and identifying relevant pre-existing knowledge for a specific research topic or patient case. 

However, this finding is not a harbinger of AI's impact on scientific discovery and therapeutics development, as Anthropic's finding is obviously scientifically useless and unremarkable at this point, and really is nothing more than IPO slop.

As Dave (CEO of $LLY) rightly notes, the really challenging part of discovering CRISPR (and other such enzymes / systems) involved understanding what the CRISPR system does and how it works. 

Evidencing this, CRISPR repeats were identified by scientists as far back as 1987 as strange oddities. However, their function was a total mystery. It wasn't until circa 2005 (almost 20 years later) that the actual purpose and function of those repeats started to become understood.  

So, all Anthropic has done here is replicate the 1987 step in finding a sequence of DNA that kind of looks like CRISPR (next to an already known reverse transcriptase and an unknown accessory protein), except this time this is even less of a novel finding because scientists have been successfully mining the bacterial genome for other CRISPR-like repeat motifs for decades, now that we know they might have some practical utility.  

Additionally, I would actually take Dave's point one step further. 

The true breakthrough in CRISPR came not just from understanding how the CRISPR system works, but creatively re-designing it and modifying in ways that actually made it useful to humans. In other words, creating a molecule that actually could affect human health from a molecule that is present in bacteria.

The initial CRISPR-cas9 system that allowed the targeted cutting of DNA in vitro was designed by Doudna and Charpentier in 2012, and won them a Nobel Prize in 2020.

Feng Zhang then built on that work to create a CRISPR-cas9 system that actually worked in human cells. 

David Liu, Andrew Anzalone, Nicole Gaudelli and others then led the development of what we might aptly call the "frontier" gene editors (e.g. $PRME, $BEAM, and via $BEAM now $LLY through the $VERV M&A).

In doing so, they used rational design and developed entirely novel techniques like PACE (more on that at the bottom of the post) to create editors from bacterial enzymes which could edit human DNA and insert / write in new DNA sequences with a high degree of specificity and efficiency, and without the dangers that are associated with CRISPR-Cas9's double strand breaks. 

It was THIS creative brilliance, in large part of a function of the engineering of an entirely novel biological design system in PACE, that represented a true revolution in human health and the ability to theoretically address a massive percentage monogenic diseases, if delivery can be solved. Indeed, it was this brilliance that has allowed two patients now with CGD to achieve what appears to be a functional cure. It was not the 1987 discovery of strange repeats.

So, to further Dave's point, not only has Anthropic not done the hard work of actual discovering what these repeats it has talked about does, they aren't even close to taking the additional step of engineering that system to actually have a differentiated benefit in human health.

Maybe they will, and if they do, I will be the first to applaud. AI has a major role to play in most aspects of society to come.

However, this touting of a big nothing burger as a major scientific discovery (especially when the average person has very limited ability to properly assess whether it is major or isn't) is another example of Anthropic appearing to be willing to say or imply things they know to be untrue to further their own hype or ends, which they then rationalization through the age old mental gymnastic of our ends justify our means. 

_______

As an interesting side note, PACE actually has degrees of parallel to the fundamental principles that make LLM's work, which I think is actually useful to abstract out as a meta-principle of high quality design and discovery systems.
 
Namely, it randomly changes an input (in PACE's case, mutating DNA sequence of the molecule being modified instead of altering a weight) and then tests the resultant output against its alignment with a desired outcome (in PACE's case the protein that is created from the mutated DNA's efficacy at executing a desired function instead of an output tokens alignment with a ground truth text), and then repeats this process extremely quickly in order to be able to trial many possible permutations of the input (in PACE's case using the rapid mutagenesis and continuous inflow and outflow system rather than GPUs). 

More simply, any discovery system that allows for extremely rapid looping of permeation of inputs, measure of output against a desired outcome, change of input predicated on degree of alignment with desired outcome will tend to be useful. 

LLM's are very useful in that regard in the right domains. 

Applying that principle in the creation of biological systems beyond PACE (atoms not bits!) is a good area to investigate for drug discovery and understanding of biological systems, whether that system is paired and augmented with AI or not.

It’s funny because when I first got really deep into generative AI, I was basically a hardcore Midjourney user. Some of my earliest followers probably still remember that.

Back then, I never seriously thought I would end up making micro-drama series with AI. Video model capabilities were still extremely limited and most AI films followed a similar format: generate a bunch of interesting shots, edit them together, then add a voiceover to make everything feel connected.

Nothing wrong with that. It just wasn’t what I wanted to make.

I wanted actual scenes. Characters talking to each other. Dialogue, comedy, mise en scene, recurring characters and some kind of continuity. I wanted to see what happened when two characters were left in a room together, not just make a montage of beautiful images.

For quite some time, the technology simply couldn’t do that reliably. The face would change, the room would change, the performance wouldn’t land or the character would suddenly become a completely different person halfway through the shot.

Then Seedance 2.0 came out and I remember thinking, damnnn, maybe I can actually do this now.

That was really the beginning of SARI & PLOY.

I had all these ideas inspired by things around me. Jakarta, Bangkok, schoolcore aesthetic, night markets, rave spaces, cheap rented rooms, neighborhood gossip, local action films, street fashion, stupid jokes and all the other things that somehow live together in my head.

Most of them would be difficult, expensive or honestly just too weird and unnecessary to produce traditionally. I can’t imagine trying to explain some of this stuff in a commercial production meeting.

But with AI, I could just try it.

I’m not doing this because I want to “revolutionize filmmaking” or make some grand statement about the future of cinema. I just finally found a way to make ideas that probably wouldn’t survive a commercial brief.

And somewhere along the way, Sari, Ploy, Sekar, Busaba and the rest of them started becoming a real part of my everyday life.

I do my normal work, go home and then start thinking about what happens to them next. What kind of trouble they get into. What Mamet sees through that stupid camera on his collar. What the next corner of their world should look like.

That part was unexpected. I thought I was experimenting with a new medium. I didn’t expect to become this attached to the characters.

I guess that’s also why MXVDXN has started making more sense to me as its own thing. A place for the ideas that are too weird, too regional, too niche, too sensual, too violent, too impractical or simply too unnecessary for my normal commercial work.

The technology will probably keep getting more expensive, which is challenging.

But right now, I’m having way too much fun making this world exist. I genuinely look forward to going home and continuing it. That’s enough reason for me to keep going.
